input.summary: Reverse § 14.2 so Customer owns paid-for Deliverables, with Vendor assignment and Vendor Technology carve-out preserved.
input.comment: [Playbook] We must own the work product we pay Vendor to create for us, so we have reversed § 14.2 to vest ownership of Deliverables in Customer with a present assignment from Vendor; a revocable, term-limited licence to our own paid-for Deliverables is not acceptable. Vendor's retained rights in Vendor Technology are unaffected (§ 14.3 and the perpetual § 13.2 licence). If Vendor cannot assign, our fallback is Vendor ownership of generic tools only, with the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable § 13.2 licence extended to the entire Deliverable.

ops.oldText: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: 14.2 Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer, and Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in each Deliverable upon creation, subject only to Vendor's retained rights in Vendor Technology under Section 14.3.
